**How it works:**
- **Line 1, `/* /* */`:** Rust allows block comments inside block comments, so it reads this as an opening comment that is still open. C++ doesn't, so for C++ the comment ends right there on line 1.
- **The C++ program** comes next. Rust ignores it because it's still inside that open comment.
- **The Rust program** is on lines that each end in `// \`. Rust's comment closes at the `*/` on the `// */ fn main() {` line, and it compiles the code after that. In C++ the `\` at the end of a line joins it to the next, so the whole Rust section becomes one long `//` comment.

**Range limit:** both versions use 128-bit unsigned integers, so the results are exact up to N=185. Above that the numbers overflow and wrap around. I made Rust wrap the same way C++ does, because otherwise `rustc`'s default build stops with an error on overflow. If you need exact results for N above 185, I'd have to add big-number arithmetic to both versions.
